title: Draft: connect canonical Relationship Engine v1 after chat save
purpose: 会話や記憶・関係性を扱う処理の変更／画面表示や操作に関する変更
purpose_basis: 変更パスと表題による分類（意味の確定には原文を確認）
body:
## Result and review status
Connect saved production conversations to Evidence → Episode → Pattern → bounded State, and feed canonical five-axis/explicit status state into the shared Relationship Interpreter and Gemini generation boundary. Lab remains synthetic and writes:false. Analysis executes after canonical chat success and cannot fail/refund a saved conversation.

**Draft; do not merge or enable production.** Updated against Draft #46 commit `e6bf2bc75aa5dd87e520724e5dbf3f4a5f0f6578` and [Sora's required review changes](https://github.com/miyazaki1016/misaki/pull/47#issuecomment-5967694565). The original distributed ownership/order/Pattern-consumption blocker is resolved by the supplied contract and passing worker/DB rollback tests. Sora acceptance review and live validation remain. The intermediate check/write gap and the legacy service_role mutation bypass are addressed by the pinned hardened contract and passing rollback tests below. This final revision changes only docs and the rollback contract test; runtime/orchestration remains unchanged.

Update commit: `42c8eba3c92e0cbaeb0825717f122e2fb3f7364a`.

## Changed files
- app/api/chat/route.ts
- lib/canonical-state.ts
- lib/relationship-acting-guide.ts
- lib/relationship-engine-v1.ts
- lib/relationship-analyzer-v1.ts
- lib/relationship-processing-v1.ts
- lib/relationship-runtime-v1.ts
- tests/relationship-engine-v1.test.ts
- tests/relationship-runtime-v1.test.cjs
- tests/relationship-distributed.rollback.sql
- tests/server-canonical.test.cjs
- tsconfig.json
- docs/RELATIONSHIP_ENGINE_V1_APPLICATION.md

## Runtime ordering / pipeline location
`chat/route.ts`: canonical relationship read → shared Interpreter → unchanged shared Gemini generator → reply validation → existing canonical chat completion → Next after() Relationship processing. Legacy emotion/turn persistence moves behind successful save. Replay schedules unfinished processing without a new generation/quota charge.
`relationship-processing-v1.ts`: DB claim of oldest unfinished post-cutover turn → renewed live ownership → canonical owned turn → critical candidate/pending/validator path → Analyzer → Evidence RPC → Episode RPC → Pattern RPC → bounded State RPC → ledger applied. No Pattern means no State RPC. The resulting State is used for subsequent responses.

## Gemini Analyzer schema
Input: canonical `{requestId,message,reply,savedAt}` only.
Output: exactly `{evidence: []}` with 0–5 strict items `{type,axis,polarity,strength,confidence,interpretation,subject,supportingTurn}`. Types: care/disclosure/repair/playful_reciprocity/harm/romantic_declaration; axes: friendship/trust/playfulness/affection/romance; polarity ±1; strength 1–100 integer; confidence 0–1; interpretation direct/ambiguous/hypothetical/quoted/third_party/negated; subject user_to_misaki/misaki_to_user/third_party; support exact user substring ≤96 characters. No status/score/delta/model write authority. Evidence payload adds supporting request/type/confidence metadata.

## RPCs
- claim_misaki_relationship_processing_v1 (#46)
- renew_misaki_relationship_processing_lease_v1 (#46)
- release_misaki_relationship_processing_lease_v1 (#46)
- advance_misaki_relationship_processing_v2 (#46)
- upsert_misaki_relationship_critical_pending_v2 (#46)
- advance_misaki_relationship_critical_pending_v2 (#46)
- record_misaki_relationship_evidence_v2
- upsert_misaki_relationship_episode_v2
- upsert_misaki_relationship_pattern_v2
- apply_misaki_relationship_state_v2 (#46, live lease token)
- apply_misaki_relationship_critical_event_v2 (#46, live lease token)
- import_misaki_temporary_relationship_v2
Existing chat completion and encrypted temporary-root writer RPCs are preserved. No direct Relationship table INSERT/UPDATE, migration or schema changes.

## Ledger retry / idempotency
Version: relationship-v1.1. Ledger identity is user/request/processing version. Failure journals the completed phase and compact candidate observations within the 2,000-character control field. Retry restores phase labels without re-executing finished operations; partial artifacts use stable Evidence/Episode/Pattern keys and existing link reads. Consumed Pattern keys come from the authoritative consumption table; DB v2 enforces once-only consumption across request IDs plus request/version replay. Recovery scans owned saved post-cutover turns chronologically, up to three per activity, stopping on failure or deferral. No background cron/queue deployment is introduced.

## Distributed ownership / lease loss
New claims own a 120-second lease. `lease_busy`, `out_of_order`, `nothing_to_process`, and replayed same-request claims defer without changing saved chat. Replayed claims return another invocation's token: this worker never adopts/releases it. A lost claim response safely waits for expiry.
Application read guards are preserved. Renew before store operations/internal paginated reads/RPC writes and before/after each external analyzer/validator. Renewal failure or v2 lease rejection stops processing without stale Evidence, pending-control, or failed-ledger writes. Every permanent data mutation now independently requires the live token in its v2 DB transaction: ledger, Evidence, Episode, Pattern, critical pending creation/update, import, State and Critical. All carry `p_processing_version`, `p_lease_token`, and the current owned `p_request_id`. Episode/Pattern ownership request is separate from historical supporting requests. The seven direct v2 implementations invoke the formal row-locking lease assertion, without delegating to revoked legacy functions; an application-side renewal is never write authority. A lease rejection during intermediate work or failed-journal write defers safely. Claim/renew/release retain the canonical contract's v1 names. Both success and abort release token-specifically in finally; release failure is best-effort and cannot fail an already-saved chat. No runtime dependency on revoked v1 final apply RPCs remains.
Permanent import is preparation inside the claimed worker, with ownership checks around pending model calls and immediately before atomic import. Canonical loading only reads import-pending status; it never starts an unclaimed import. Until import completes, generation uses the current canonical row with pending status constraints.

## Deterministic policy for review
Only direct user→Misaki evidence with confidence ≥0.8 and strength ≥50 can become an Episode. One intention per Tokyo day; confession paraphrases share one Episode across days. Three independent days produce a Pattern; each batch votes ±1, with aggregate per-axis ±3 bound. No raw turn-count growth. This conservative application policy needs Sora's semantic review.

## Critical Events
Separate explicit candidate detection, durable pending before external validator, validated facts via atomic Event/Status RPC. Exact user supporting substring required; explicit mutual acceptance needed for partner status. Dismissed/failed paths use #46 pending controls. Score cannot establish partnership; breakup preserves historical axes; reconciliation does not restore partnership. Recent saved turns bridge pending creation delay into the next Resolver constraint.

## State supply / anonymous / Lab
Permanent canonical axes/status are read directly, and legacy points map only intimacy. Explicit partner status takes precedence even at zero romance. Old point-based relationship guide is omitted while v1 enabled.
Anonymous snapshots/pending/trajectory stay inside encrypted revision-checked server roots. Supporting canonical pairs inside the root are required; no incremental anonymous plaintext Evidence writes. After permanent auth, the claimed post-save worker imports the newest verified frozen snapshot exactly once, finishing pending analysis in memory with lease checks before the import RPC. Import failure does not break ordinary history restoration and prevents permanent v1 processing from racing ahead.
Lab keeps writes:false and the same Interpreter/generator. Body Clock code and expiry/quota/history/memory/email-save/device specifications are unchanged.

## Tests
- Existing regression: 176/176 pass.
- Relationship tests: 73/73 pass; full suite 249/249. The final ACL-contract revision adds DB privilege/invocation checks; all existing Relationship and regression tests were rerun.
- TypeScript noEmit, production Next build, git diff --check: pass.
- New tests pause intermediate writes after a successful application guard, then expire/reclaim ownership before the DB-contract write: stale ledger/Evidence/Episode/Pattern/critical pending create+update/import are rejected with zero writes. Live-token RPC argument/schema tests cover current ownership identity. Import preserves lease-rejection errors. Failed-journal rejection is a nonfatal deferral.
- Existing multi-worker cases pass: stale State/Critical, cross-request Pattern consumption, request processing order, expiry/reclaim, token-specific stale release, competing explicit acceptance/breakup, release failure, guarded import and saved-chat isolation.
- Installed DB `tests/relationship-distributed.rollback.sql`: PASS in BEGIN/ROLLBACK under service_role, with a real 30-second lease and 31-second expiry wait before re-claim. All nine mutation types reject the stale token, including pending creation and updating an existing pending row, and import. Import receipt and pending status are asserted unchanged. Fresh-token ledger/Evidence/Episode/Pattern/pending wrappers succeed; State replay, ±3 bound, Pattern guard, cross-request double-consumption prevention and claim ordering/busy/replay/release checks pass.
- Hardened ACL contract: all nine legacy permanent mutation v1 RPCs are EXECUTE-denied for service_role; all nine corresponding v2 RPCs are EXECUTE-permitted. Rollback tests assert both privilege sets and actually invoke every legacy v1 with typed NULL arguments: all must raise SQLSTATE 42501 (insufficient_privilege), proving lease fencing cannot be bypassed through legacy entry points. The existing v2 stale-token/invalid-token rejection checks and live-token intermediate success checks pass against the direct implementations.
- All nine tracked fixture categories are zero after rollback. During the expiry wait only unique test-version lease/artifact locks are held; no canonical State lock or State mutation precedes the wait. No direct INSERT/UPDATE, DDL, model call or persistent fixture is used.
- Lab writes:false/shared generation and quota/history/memory/Body Clock/anonymous boundary/retry/permanence/email-save/device regression tests pass.
- Exact-head GitHub CI [run #318](https://github.com/miyazaki1016/misaki/actions/runs/37115734824): success on `42c8eba3c92e0cbaeb0825717f122e2fb3f7364a` (npm test and production build steps both successful).
- Exact-head Vercel Preview: READY at https://misaki-g23bq52ev-kishibojim.vercel.app (deployment `dpl_9JJgWu9jikwbrnHiEd6M21Vfri6z`, preview target). HTTP: `/` 200, `/chat` 200, GET `/api/acting-lab` 405. Signed-in/live Gemini/device journeys remain for the next validation stage.
- Deterministic worker tests use separate instances over a shared DB-contract model. Live Gemini classification quality, signed-in cross-device journeys and actual multi-instance Vercel traffic with the engine enabled remain unverified.

## Production DB changes
No persistent changes and no DDL. Only read-only contract inspection and rollback-only RPC validation. Production/Preview enablement variables have not been modified.

## Remaining validation
1. Sora's policy/DB/safety review; signed-in Preview, live Gemini and cross-device real journeys; real multi-instance Vercel traffic with the gate enabled.
2. Recovery remains opportunistic on successful/replayed chat activity; no autonomous queue/cron has been added.
3. Broader Body Clock Reply Core convergence is outside the no-Body-Clock-change scope.

The original missing distributed contract blocker is resolved after the required tests above passed. Neither PR has been merged and no production enablement has occurred. Details: docs/RELATIONSHIP_ENGINE_V1_APPLICATION.md.

@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+# Relationship Engine v1 application integration
+
+Status: review draft, not a production cutover. Uses updated Draft PR #46 at `e6bf2bc75aa5dd87e520724e5dbf3f4a5f0f6578` as the formal distributed-worker DB contract. No migration or DB definition changes are included.
+
+## Runtime boundary
+
+`app/api/chat/route.ts` loads canonical state, feeds the shared Interpreter, generates/validates using the unchanged shared Gemini JSON generator, and commits through the existing permanent/temporary chat RPC. Only successful commit/replay schedules `next/server.after()` processing. Legacy emotion/turn writes also occur after success, with failures isolated from the already-committed quota receipt.
+
+The just-completed turn affects a subsequent response, not its own pre-save generation. This follows the canonical handoff's post-save ordering. Lab continues supplying synthetic profiles to the same Interpreter and generator with `writes:false`.
+
+`lib/canonical-state.ts` reads five axes and explicit status directly from the server row. Legacy points determine only intimacy stage. The Interpreter gives explicit partner status precedence even at zero romance. During v1 operation the old point-based relationship guide is omitted. Pending critical context takes precedence over asserting an established/continuing relationship; recent saved turns bridge the interval before the background worker creates pending rows.
+
+## Enablement
+
+Both the intended processing version and a valid cutover timestamp are needed:
+
+```
+MISAKI_RELATIONSHIP_ENGINE_VERSION=relationship-v1.1
+MISAKI_RELATIONSHIP_ENGINE_START_AT=<explicit ISO timestamp selected for rollout>
+```
+
+Neither has been set by this implementation. Keep the gate off until Sora/owner acceptance review and explicit rollout authorization. Historical turns before the selected boundary are not analyzed with a new model version. Do not move the timestamp backward to rewrite history.
+
+## Analyzer schema
+
+Input is a canonical saved `Turn`: `requestId`, `message`, `reply`, `savedAt`. The model receives it as untrusted data. No Lab, browser-supplied history or other user's turn enters this boundary.
+
+Output is exactly `{evidence: Evidence[]}` (0–5 items), where each item has:
+
+| Field | Contract |
+| --- | --- |
+| type | care, disclosure, repair, playful_reciprocity, harm, romantic_declaration |
+| axis | friendship, trust, playfulness, affection, romance |
+| polarity | -1 or +1 |
+| strength | integer 1–100 |
+| confidence | finite number 0–1 |
+| interpretation | direct, ambiguous, hypothetical, quoted, third_party, negated |
+| subject | user_to_misaki, misaki_to_user, third_party |
+| supportingTurn | exact user-message substring, 1–96 characters |
+
+Unknown fields (including scores, status, delta) and fabricated support are rejected. The RPC payload also records the canonical supporting request, Evidence type and confidence. Generated Misaki text alone cannot qualify for an Episode.
+
+The conservative initial Episode/Pattern policy is an application policy for review: only direct user→Misaki evidence at confidence ≥0.8 and strength ≥50 qualifies. An intention/type/axis/polarity is grouped at most once per Tokyo day; romantic declarations share one Episode across days/paraphrases. Three independent days form a Pattern; each three-day batch is consumed once. A confirmed Pattern votes ±1 and combined per-axis delta is clamped to ±3. No Pattern means no State RPC, including no version-only update. DB's bounded State RPC remains the final authority for permanent state.
+
+## RPCs and retry
+
+`lib/relationship-processing-v1.ts` owns orchestration and RPC-only permanent writes:
+
+- claim_misaki_relationship_processing_v1
+- renew_misaki_relationship_processing_lease_v1
+- release_misaki_relationship_processing_lease_v1
+- advance_misaki_relationship_processing_v2
+- record_misaki_relationship_evidence_v2
+- upsert_misaki_relationship_episode_v2
+- upsert_misaki_relationship_pattern_v2
+- apply_misaki_relationship_state_v2
+- upsert_misaki_relationship_critical_pending_v2
+- advance_misaki_relationship_critical_pending_v2
+- apply_misaki_relationship_critical_event_v2
+
+`lib/relationship-runtime-v1.ts` additionally uses `import_misaki_temporary_relationship_v2` at permanence and the existing encrypted-root writer for anonymous post-save processing. Chat's existing completion RPCs remain unchanged.
+
+Before processing or importing permanent Relationship data, the worker claims the oldest unfinished post-cutover request under the DB's per-user/version lease. `lease_busy`, `out_of_order`, `nothing_to_process`, and a replayed same-request claim are deferrals. A replayed claim returns an existing token; this invocation does **not** adopt or release that token. This prevents two same-request workers from sharing ownership. A lost claim response waits for expiry/reclaim.
+
+A newly acquired token is renewed before each store operation, each internal paginated DB read/write, and before/after each external analyzer or validator call. Lease duration is 120 seconds; analyzer calls retain the separate 10-second/no-retry analysis budget. Renewal errors conservatively stop processing. No stale model result, pending status, or failed ledger journal is written after observed lease loss. All nine permanent data mutation paths use v2 RPCs with explicit `p_processing_version`, `p_lease_token`, and the current owned `p_request_id`, independently checked inside the DB write transaction. Episode/Pattern ownership uses the current processing request, even when the supporting Episode comes from an earlier request. Import receives the same owned request/token as ordinary processing. The direct v2 intermediate mutations lock the lease row and check its current expiry through the formal assert helper; an application renewal is never treated as sufficient write authorization. Claim/renew/release keep their formally specified v1 names. Reads retain application-side guards. Any intermediate/import/failure-journal DB lease rejection is a nonfatal deferral; no subsequent failed-ledger write is attempted. Consumed Patterns are read from `misaki_relationship_pattern_consumptions`; DB enforces consumption once across request IDs. Both successful and aborted owners release in `finally`; token-specific stale release cannot delete a replacement lease. Release errors remain isolated from saved chat.
+
+The ledger is keyed by user/request/processing version. Completed phases are skipped. Failure records a compact sanitized journal containing the last completed phase and candidate observations; the journal fits the control RPC's 2,000-character field. Recovery performs the explicit failed→analyzing control transition, restores completed phase labels without rerunning their operations, and continues. Partial writes are found by stable keys and links. State success followed by ledger failure is recovered through the application audit/consumed Pattern set and request/version replay guard.
+
+Failures never refund/fail a committed chat. Successful/replayed chat schedules recovery; the worker processes at most three unfinished post-cutover turns chronologically and stops at the first failure or deferral. This is opportunistic retry on user activity, not a continuously running queue worker. Queries page beyond Supabase's default response limit.
+
+## Critical Events
+
+Critical candidates are detected independently from ordinary Evidence using conservative explicit user language. Quoted/hypothetical/third-party text is excluded. Candidate context is saved before an external validator call. The validator emits only `confirmed` and an exact supporting user substring; acceptance must represent explicit mutual agreement, not affection/score/proposal alone. Confirmed facts use the atomic critical RPC. Rejected candidates are dismissed through the pending-control RPC; validator failures stay failed/pending for retry. The critical RPC removes resolved pending rows. Reconciliation never automatically restores partner status; breakup does not zero historical axes.
+
+## Anonymous continuity
+
+The encrypted server-root payload carries `relationshipEngine`: state, version, compact episodes, consumed Pattern keys, processed requests, pending canonical turns and explicit critical events. Queue entries are sealed as part of successful canonical temporary-turn completion. Analysis verifies supporting user/assistant pairs inside the current root and writes through the existing revision-checked root writer. No anonymous Evidence/Episode/Pattern is incrementally written to permanent plaintext tables. First post-cutover processing materializes the snapshot before ordinary permanent analysis; until then, generation uses the current canonical row and avoids asserting pending status transitions.

+- Relationship tests: 73/73 pass (249 total). This final ACL-contract revision adds DB rollback privilege/invocation checks and reruns all existing tests.
+- TypeScript noEmit and Next production build: pass.

Real calls to every legacy v1 function must raise SQLSTATE 42501 (insufficient_privilege), proving the unleased bypass is closed. # Relationship Engine v1 application integration

Status: review draft, not a production cutover. Uses updated Draft PR #46 at `e6bf2bc75aa5dd87e520724e5dbf3f4a5f0f6578` as the formal distributed-worker DB contract. No migration or DB definition changes are included.

## Runtime boundary

`app/api/chat/route.ts` loads canonical state, feeds the shared Interpreter, generates/validates using the unchanged shared Gemini JSON generator, and commits through the existing permanent/temporary chat RPC. Only successful commit/replay schedules `next/server.after()` processing. Legacy emotion/turn writes also occur after success, with failures isolated from the already-committed quota receipt.

The just-completed turn affects a subsequent response, not its own pre-save generation. This follows the canonical handoff's post-save ordering. Lab continues supplying synthetic profiles to the same Interpreter and generator with `writes:false`.

`lib/canonical-state.ts` reads five axes and explicit status directly from the server row. Legacy points determine only intimacy stage. The Interpreter gives explicit partner status precedence even at zero romance. During v1 operation the old point-based relationship guide is omitted. Pending critical context takes precedence over asserting an established/continuing relationship; recent saved turns bridge the interval before the background worker creates pending rows.

## Enablement

Both the intended processing version and a valid cutover timestamp are needed:

```
MISAKI_RELATIONSHIP_ENGINE_VERSION=relationship-v1.1
MISAKI_RELATIONSHIP_ENGINE_START_AT=<explicit ISO timestamp selected for rollout>
```

Neither has been set by this implementation. Keep the gate off until Sora/owner acceptance review and explicit rollout authorization. Historical turns before the selected boundary are not analyzed with a new model version. Do not move the timestamp backward to rewrite history.

## Analyzer schema

Input is a canonical saved `Turn`: `requestId`, `message`, `reply`, `savedAt`. The model receives it as untrusted data. No Lab, browser-supplied history or other user's turn enters this boundary.

Output is exactly `{evidence: Evidence[]}` (0–5 items), where each item has:

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| type | care, disclosure, repair, playful_reciprocity, harm, romantic_declaration |
| axis | friendship, trust, playfulness, affection, romance |
| polarity | -1 or +1 |
| strength | integer 1–100 |
| confidence | finite number 0–1 |
| interpretation | direct, ambiguous, hypothetical, quoted, third_party, negated |
| subject | user_to_misaki, misaki_to_user, third_party |
| supportingTurn | exact user-message substring, 1–96 characters |

Unknown fields (including scores, status, delta) and fabricated support are rejected. The RPC payload also records the canonical supporting request, Evidence type and confidence. Generated Misaki text alone cannot qualify for an Episode.

The conservative initial Episode/Pattern policy is an application policy for review: only direct user→Misaki evidence at confidence ≥0.8 and strength ≥50 qualifies. An intention/type/axis/polarity is grouped at most once per Tokyo day; romantic declarations share one Episode across days/paraphrases. Three independent days form a Pattern; each three-day batch is consumed once. A confirmed Pattern votes ±1 and combined per-axis delta is clamped to ±3. No Pattern means no State RPC, including no version-only update. DB's bounded State RPC remains the final authority for permanent state.

## RPCs and retry

`lib/relationship-processing-v1.ts` owns orchestration and RPC-only permanent writes:

- claim_misaki_relationship_processing_v1
- renew_misaki_relationship_processing_lease_v1
- release_misaki_relationship_processing_lease_v1
- advance_misaki_relationship_processing_v2
- record_misaki_relationship_evidence_v2
- upsert_misaki_relationship_episode_v2
- upsert_misaki_relationship_pattern_v2
- apply_misaki_relationship_state_v2
- upsert_misaki_relationship_critical_pending_v2
- advance_misaki_relationship_critical_pending_v2
- apply_misaki_relationship_critical_event_v2

`lib/relationship-runtime-v1.ts` additionally uses `import_misaki_temporary_relationship_v2` at permanence and the existing encrypted-root writer for anonymous post-save processing. Chat's existing completion RPCs remain unchanged.

Before processing or importing permanent Relationship data, the worker claims the oldest unfinished post-cutover request under the DB's per-user/version lease. `lease_busy`, `out_of_order`, `nothing_to_process`, and a replayed same-request claim are deferrals. A replayed claim returns an existing token; this invocation does **not** adopt or release that token. This prevents two same-request workers from sharing ownership. A lost claim response waits for expiry/reclaim.

A newly acquired token is renewed before each store operation, each internal paginated DB read/write, and before/after each external analyzer or validator call. Lease duration is 120 seconds; analyzer calls retain the separate 10-second/no-retry analysis budget. Renewal errors conservatively stop processing. No stale model result, pending status, or failed ledger journal is written after observed lease loss. All nine permanent data mutation paths use v2 RPCs with explicit `p_processing_version`, `p_lease_token`, and the current owned `p_request_id`, independently checked inside the DB write transaction. Episode/Pattern ownership uses the current processing request, even when the supporting Episode comes from an earlier request. Import receives the same owned request/token as ordinary processing. The direct v2 intermediate mutations lock the lease row and check its current expiry through the formal assert helper; an application renewal is never treated as sufficient write authorization. Claim/renew/release keep their formally specified v1 names. Reads retain application-side guards. Any intermediate/import/failure-journal DB lease rejection is a nonfatal deferral; no subsequent failed-ledger write is attempted. Consumed Patterns are read from `misaki_relationship_pattern_consumptions`; DB enforces consumption once across request IDs. Both successful and aborted owners release in `finally`; token-specific stale release cannot delete a replacement lease. Release errors remain isolated from saved chat.

The ledger is keyed by user/request/processing version. Completed phases are skipped. Failure records a compact sanitized journal containing the last completed phase and candidate observations; the journal fits the control RPC's 2,000-character field. Recovery performs the explicit failed→analyzing control transition, restores completed phase labels without rerunning their operations, and continues. Partial writes are found by stable keys and links. State success followed by ledger failure is recovered through the application audit/consumed Pattern set and request/version replay guard.

Failures never refund/fail a committed chat. Successful/replayed chat schedules recovery; the worker processes at most three unfinished post-cutover turns chronologically and stops at the first failure or deferral. This is opportunistic retry on user activity, not a continuously running queue worker. Queries page beyond Supabase's default response limit.

## Critical Events

Critical candidates are detected independently from ordinary Evidence using conservative explicit user language. Quoted/hypothetical/third-party text is excluded. Candidate context is saved before an external validator call. The validator emits only `confirmed` and an exact supporting user substring; acceptance must represent explicit mutual agreement, not affection/score/proposal alone. Confirmed facts use the atomic critical RPC. Rejected candidates are dismissed through the pending-control RPC; validator failures stay failed/pending for retry. The critical RPC removes resolved pending rows. Reconciliation never automatically restores partner status; breakup does not zero historical axes.

## Anonymous continuity

The encrypted server-root payload carries `relationshipEngine`: state, version, compact episodes, consumed Pattern keys, processed requests, pending canonical turns and explicit critical events. Queue entries are sealed as part of successful canonical temporary-turn completion. Analysis verifies supporting user/assistant pairs inside the current root and writes through the existing revision-checked root writer. No anonymous Evidence/Episode/Pattern is incrementally written to permanent plaintext tables. Existing Body Clock spread of the encrypted payload preserves the snapshot without generating positive Evidence or extending expiry.

Email save is not made into an early one-time import. After auth becomes permanent, the latest verified frozen root is imported once under the post-save worker’s claimed lease; any pending analysis is finished in memory before the atomic import because the anonymous writer correctly rejects permanent accounts. Failed import/analysis is retryable and blocks subsequent permanent v1 processing, while ordinary conversation/history restoration still succeeds. Old snapshots cannot overwrite an already-recorded import. Canonical state loading is read-only: it detects an outstanding frozen-root import and marks relationship context pending. It never starts an unclaimed import. First post-cutover processing materializes the snapshot before ordinary permanent analysis; until then, generation uses the current canonical row and avoids asserting pending status transitions.

## Verification

- Existing tests: 176/176 pass.
- Relationship tests: 73/73 pass (249 total). This final ACL-contract revision adds DB rollback privilege/invocation checks and reruns all existing tests.
- TypeScript noEmit and Next production build: pass.
- Multi-worker application tests use independent store instances over one shared DB-contract model, explicit barriers, and a controlled clock: same-user/request races, oldest unfinished ordering, lease expiry/reclaim, stale State/critical rejection, cross-request Pattern consumption, competing acceptance/breakup transitions, renewal loss, release failure, guarded import, and saved-chat failure isolation pass. Additional tests pause each intermediate RPC after the application guard has succeeded, expire/reclaim ownership, and verify rejection at the DB-contract boundary with zero writes. Live-token schema checks cover all six intermediate adapters; import carries the same identity and preserves the DB lease-rejection reason. These are deterministic orchestration tests, not live multi-process Vercel tests.
- `tests/relationship-distributed.rollback.sql` ran successfully against the installed DB contract in one BEGIN/ROLLBACK transaction using service_role. It reads existing canonical turn IDs without reading message contents; all fixture writes use RPCs. Checks: out-of-order/busy/replayed claims, renewal, real expiry/reclaim, token-specific stale release, rejection of stale ledger/Evidence/Episode/Pattern/critical pending creation+update/import/State/Critical, invalid State/critical tokens, ±3 bound, Pattern requirement, same-request State replay, cross-request Pattern consumption. Import receipt is asserted unchanged; stale artifacts and pending status remain unchanged. Fresh-token intermediate mutations also succeed. The rollback contract now asserts service_role EXECUTE denied on all nine legacy v1 mutations and permitted on all nine matching v2 mutations. Real calls to every legacy v1 function must raise SQLSTATE 42501 (insufficient_privilege), proving the unleased bypass is closed. All nine tracked fixture categories were verified zero after rollback. No persistent DB/schema change.
- The DB check uses a 30-second lease and waits 31 seconds before reclaiming. During this wait it holds only unique test-version lease/artifact locks; no canonical State row lock or State mutation precedes the wait. No direct table INSERT/UPDATE or DDL is used.
- Lab writes:false, shared generator boundary and existing quota/history/memory/Body Clock/email-save/device regressions pass.
- Actual Gemini classification quality and signed-in cross-device Preview journeys still require Sora/owner evaluation; mocked generator tests do not establish live model quality.

## Distributed blocker resolution and remaining review

The original missing worker ownership/order/Pattern-consumption contract is resolved by the updated PR #46 contract, token-fenced application integration, and the passing multi-worker/DB rollback tests above. The intermediate check/write TOCTOU identified in the second review is addressed by the seven token-fenced v2 mutations in the pinned contract, and the passing tests above. The final DB hardening removes service_role execution of every legacy v1 data mutation; direct v2 implementations no longer delegate to those revoked functions. No legacy permanent data mutation v1 RPC is called from application runtime; v1 names are retained only for the formal claim/renew/release control APIs. The application runtime and orchestration are unchanged in this final ACL-contract revision.

The PR remains Draft and production enablement remains off. Sora still reviews the policy and safety boundaries. Live Gemini classification quality, signed-in cross-device Preview journeys, and actual Vercel multi-instance traffic have not been exercised with the engine enabled. Recovery remains opportunistic on successful/replayed chat activity; there is no newly introduced queue or autonomous retry scheduler.

Body Clock generation architecture is unchanged per this task's no-Body-Clock-change constraint; broader multi-channel Reply Core convergence is not claimed.

comments.body:
Sora review checkpoint — distributed worker contract is now available in updated Draft PR #46.

Please update this PR against the new DB contract before further acceptance review.

Required changes:
1. Claim processing ownership before any permanent Relationship Engine work with `claim_misaki_relationship_processing_v1`.
2. Treat `lease_busy` / `out_of_order` as non-fatal deferral, not chat failure.
3. Renew the lease before long external work if needed; stop processing immediately on lease loss.
4. Use only `apply_misaki_relationship_state_v2` with the live lease token.
5. Use only `apply_misaki_relationship_critical_event_v2` with the live lease token.
6. Release the lease on successful completion and best-effort on aborted processing. Release failure must not affect an already-saved chat.
7. Remove runtime dependency on legacy final apply v1 RPCs; service_role execution has been revoked.
8. Add distributed tests for:
   - two workers racing for the same user,
   - later request before oldest unfinished request,
   - lease expiry and reclaim,
   - stale worker final mutation rejection,
   - same Pattern attempted by different request IDs,
   - critical transitions under competing workers.
9. Keep the engine enablement gate off. Do not merge or enable production.
10. Update docs/PR body so the original distributed blocker is considered resolved only after these tests pass.

DB rollback verification already passed for out-of-order claim rejection, cross-request Pattern double-consumption rejection, and invalid lease rejection.

Sora second review checkpoint — one remaining distributed-safety gap was found and the DB contract has now been strengthened in Draft PR #46 (latest commit `5d25f30d2fdaa4d3c38f16561c295a125f2b5a8a`).

Why this matters:
The current PR fences final State/Critical writes, but intermediate Evidence/Episode/Pattern/ledger/critical-pending/import writes still rely on a renew-before-write application check. That leaves a theoretical renew→write TOCTOU window if a lease expires and is reclaimed between those two operations.

PR #46 now provides lease-token-fenced v2 wrappers for every permanent mutation, validating and locking the lease row in the same DB transaction as the write.

Please update PR #47 to use:
- `advance_misaki_relationship_processing_v2`
- `record_misaki_relationship_evidence_v2`
- `upsert_misaki_relationship_episode_v2`
- `upsert_misaki_relationship_pattern_v2`
- `upsert_misaki_relationship_critical_pending_v2`
- `advance_misaki_relationship_critical_pending_v2`
- `import_misaki_temporary_relationship_v2`
- existing `apply_misaki_relationship_state_v2`
- existing `apply_misaki_relationship_critical_event_v2`

All mutation calls must pass the live `processing_version + lease_token`. Reads may remain application-guarded.

Add tests proving that after lease expiry/reclaim, a stale worker cannot write:
1. ledger phase/error,
2. Evidence,
3. Episode,
4. Pattern,
5. critical pending state,
6. permanent import,
in addition to the already-covered final State/Critical rejection.

Keep Draft, gate OFF, no merge, no production enablement.

Sora final DB hardening checkpoint.

Application code at commit `184c77b5ac75d823e06f5f31cb2f26aad396fdd4` correctly uses the lease-fenced v2 mutation APIs, and CI #315 is green.

One DB-contract bypass was found during final acceptance review: the legacy intermediate/import v1 RPCs were still executable by service_role even though runtime no longer called them. That could allow a future regression to bypass lease fencing.

This has now been closed in Draft PR #46. Latest DB-contract commit:
`e6bf2bc75aa5dd87e520724e5dbf3f4a5f0f6578`

Production verification:
- all legacy permanent Relationship mutation v1 RPCs: service_role EXECUTE = false
- corresponding v2 RPCs: service_role EXECUTE = true
- v2 implementations contain their canonical write logic directly and do not depend on calling v1
- Security Advisor shows no new SECURITY DEFINER exposure

PR #47 does not need orchestration changes for this hardening because it already calls only v2 mutations. Please:
1. pin docs/PR body to PR #46 commit `e6bf2bc75aa5dd87e520724e5dbf3f4a5f0f6578`,
2. add/extend the DB rollback contract test to assert service_role cannot execute the legacy v1 mutation RPCs and can execute the v2 replacements,
3. rerun full tests/CI,
4. keep Draft + gate OFF; do not merge or enable production.

After that, code/DB acceptance can move to live Gemini + authenticated Preview/device + actual multi-instance validation.

Sora acceptance checkpoint — code + DB contract accepted.

Verified at PR #47 commit `42c8eba3c92e0cbaeb0825717f122e2fb3f7364a`:
- final revision changes only docs + rollback DB contract test; runtime/orchestration unchanged
- full suite 249/249
- TypeScript / production build / diff check pass
- exact-head GitHub CI #318 success
- PR #46 pinned to DB contract commit `e6bf2bc75aa5dd87e520724e5dbf3f4a5f0f6578`
- legacy permanent Relationship mutation v1 EXECUTE denied 9/9 for service_role
- corresponding v2 mutation EXECUTE allowed 9/9
- live-lease fencing / stale-worker rejection / Pattern once-only consumption / ordering / retry boundaries covered by application + rollback DB tests
- no persistent DB fixture remains

Code/DB acceptance blocker is closed.

Do not merge or enable production yet. Keep Draft + production gate OFF.

Next validation stage:
1. live Gemini Analyzer/critical-validator quality,
2. authenticated Preview journey,
3. cross-device continuity,
4. actual Vercel multi-instance contention/lease behavior.

Any failure in those stages should return here as a new acceptance blocker before merge/cutover.
